newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI Octava to finance investment internally.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI Octava to finance investment internally.

text.p: Polish National Investment Fund No. 8, or Octava, wants to finance its investments internally but a new issue is possible if its own funds prove insufficient, the president of the firm managing the fund said on Tuesday.
Martin Miszerak, president of KP Konsorcjum, said at a news conference that the fund did not plan to use bank loans to finance its investments.

"We don't plan to use bank loans. We will be investing our own funds, which would come from selling shares. If they prove too small, we don't rule out a share capital rise," he said without elaborating.
He added the fund wanted to sell most of its minority stakes.
Miszerak also said 40 percent of the value of Octava's portfolio were companies of high growth potential.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

Beginning May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought participation units in the scheme have been able to exchange each of them for 15 shares, one in each fund. On Thursday, shares of the funds will start trade on the Warsaw bourse.
